rv.q: It is not nearly as high-powered in its special effects as a Disney adaptation but just as dazzling in its magic realism.
If you're an admirer of Hayao Miyazaki's Studio Ghibli movies, you're almost certain to feel the same about Tom Morton-Smith's puppet-driven adaptation
For all the ravishing imagery and the collective endeavour involved, this show isn't quirky or adult-friendly enough for that.
It’s unadulterated joy: a huge, healing hug of a show, generous and utterly beguiling.
But every setpiece you're willing to be a stunner, is a stunner, an endless cavalcade of sweet, strange joy.
Full of spirit, heart and overall truly enchanting, My Neighbour Totoro really is a magical creature of a show.
Overall, this is a warm bath of a production guaranteed to delight families and adults with its ingenious, continuously revolving and evolving staging.
Non-Ghibli–o-philes may be bored and bewildered, but the beautiful design, musical loveliness and warm tone are just enough to make My Neighbour Totoro a pleasant evening.
There were a considerable number of families with younger children in the audience, who will doubtless love every moment and be oblivious to the creators' urge to explore guilt issues.
